content: Kwale County Governor Fatuma Achani Monday led a section of legislators in a charm offensive to rally residents behind President William Ruto’s re-election bid ahead of the 2027 General Election.
The four legislators included Matuga MP Kassim Tandaza, Msambweni MP Feisal Abdallah, Lungalunga MP Mangale Chiforomodo and Kinango MP Gonzi Rai.

Speaking during UDA grassroots delegates meeting at Mwachema Primary School in Tiwi Ward, Matuga Sub-County, Achani urged residents to support President Ruto’s 2027 re-election bid, citing infrastructure and socio-economic projects undertaken by the Kenya Kwanza administration in Kwale County and the wider Coast region.

Achani said the administration had addressed longstanding land disputes and the squatter crisis in the Coast region through the issuance of more than 94,000 title deeds in Kwale County, challenges she said previous administrations had failed to resolve.

“It is only Ruto’s administration that has sorted out the land disputes and squatters crisis in the Coast Region through issuance of over 94, 000 title deeds in Kwale, something that previous administrations failed to solve .”Achani Said.

She cited the construction of the Kwale–Kinango road, Shimoni Port and Mwachande Bridge, as well as the establishment of the National Mariculture Training Centre, as key development projects initiated under President Ruto’s administration.
The MPs echoed the Governor’s sentiments, accusing opposition leaders of lacking a clear development agenda.

Bad day in office for Wetang’ula as he hangs on Farouk’s coat tails for political survival
items.description: The political stars appear to have aligned against Wetang'ula and his party.
content: National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula is practically fighting for political survival in the Kenyan political space.
Wetangula might previously have been a man of all seasons. But seemingly not for the coming one.
For more than one year now, matters have been turning topsy-turvy for the 69-year-old Senior Counsel.
The going is noticeably going very tough for the Ford Kenya Party Leader.

Both at national and regional levels, the former Sirisia MP is seemingly swimming against the political tides and is literally hanging on the coat-tails of President William Ruto’s personal assistant Farouk Kibet.
For more than one year now, Wetang’ula has been striding across the political terrains of Western, with Farouk in tow, advancing the case for Ruto’s re-election next year.
READ ALSO : Lusaka next? Anxiety grows as Ford Kenya cracks widen, top officials abandon Wetang’ula
Within that period, Wetang’ula has been embroiled in court cases, a political rebellion from his own family, county and political party.

Last year, some members of the civil society took the self-proclaimed Papa Wa Roma to court, demanding his removal as the Ford Kenya Party Leader, arguing that as umpire of a multi-party Legislature, his position in the political outfit is untenable since it is prone to conflict of interest.

Early this year, Wetang’ula himself threatened to sue the Standard Media Group after one of its publication, The Standard, splashed an article in which it reported that most of the senior public servants from his Bukusu community and Bungoma and Trans-Nzoia counties are his blood relatives who owe their appointments directly to him..

For more than one year now, Wetang’ula has been campaigning, using parliamentarians from the Western region to do the spade work, to be appointed as Ruto’s running-mate, a move that appears to have floundered.
The political stars appear to have aligned against Wetang’ula and his party.
Slightly more than eight months to the next General-Election, Wetang’ula is noticeably in a very precarious position.
Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna who, like Wetang’ula , hails from Bungoma county, has sprung onto the national political arena and driven the Speaker to the back burner of regional politics.

Sifuna has attracted considerable national attention after he announced his departure from the popular Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) after being ejected as the party’s secretary-general, has since launched the Linda Mwananchi Movement (LMM) from where he is expected to run for Presidency.

The rise of Sifuna, coupled with previous persistent attacks from Trans-Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, have pushed Wetang’ula into a tight corner from where he is now fighting for both space and relevance in his own home turf.

Wetang’ula, through his Ford Kenya party mobilised more than 200, 000 votes for Ruto’s presidential candidature in 2022 from Bungoma County, the highest number in any of the five Mulembe Nation counties.
READ ALSO: FORD-K headed for collapse, Wetang’ula under siege

Wetang’ula’s critics argue that his refusal to relinquish the Ford Kenya leadership portrays him as a sympathizer of the Opposition, a claim that has been insinuated by Nandi Senator Samson Cherargei who early this year warned the Speaker not to dream of being supported again by UDA if he did not merge the outfit with UDA in the same manner that Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi did in 2024 with his former party, the Amani National Congress (ANC).

The critics maintain that the failure by Wetang’ula’s party to field a candidate for the post of Bungoma governor in the 2027 polls elections, in addition to the fact that his young brother, Tim Wanyonyi who is the MP for Westlands on an ODM ticket is contesting for the same seat on Sifuna’s LMM exposes him as an usher of the Opposition into Bukusuland.
Ford Kenya has for the better part of this year been engulfed fierce internal feuds that have sparked an exodus of officials from the party.
The departure leaves the Speaker in a very vulnerable position. it is against this background that Wetangula has been left to cavort unendingly around Farouk Kibet

items.description: Kasuku has unveiled a refreshed identity and “Dream. Learn. Become.” in Nairobi, with Share Your Dream marking its shift beyond stationery for Kenyan children.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

Kasuku, the stationery brand that has been a fixture in Kenyan classrooms for over six decades, has relaunched with a new brand identity and positioning line, signalling a strategic shift from product supplier to purpose-led education brand.
The relaunch took place on November 12, 2026, at the Mövenpick Hotel in Westlands, Nairobi, in the presence of media, education stakeholders, and partners.
The event was organised by Twiga Stationers & Printers Ltd, the company that owns the Kasuku brand.
Chief executive Asitha Samaraweera framed the rebrand as both a continuation of the brand's heritage and a deliberate expansion of its story.

The updated visual identity retains the brand's core product promise of quality stationery, but the more significant change is in how the brand presents itself.
The new tagline, "Dream. Learn. Become", is built around a three-stage narrative tied to childhood development.
As part of the rebrand, Kasuku announced an upcoming initiative called Share Your Dream, which will invite children across Kenya to share their aspirations and encourage one another.

The company described it as an early expression of its wider purpose, though no launch date, format, or delivery channel has been confirmed.
The pivot towards purpose-led engagement is a familiar strategy among consumer brands competing for the loyalty of parents, teachers, and learners.
For Kasuku, it also offers a way to differentiate itself from cheaper, unbranded stationery imports that have put pressure on margins across the sector.
Kenya's stationery market is competitive, with brands contending on price, quality, availability, and emotional relevance, particularly during the back-to-school season.

A heritage brand carries the advantage of recognition and trust, but those qualities must be actively converted into shelf presence and consumer preference in an environment where supermarkets, wholesalers, and online retailers all stock rival products.
The company has not disclosed the cost of the rebrand, any sales targets, or plans for expansion into new markets.
How effectively Kasuku translates its new positioning into consistent products and community programmes will ultimately determine whether the relaunch delivers lasting results.

In other news, Mitumba flipping, street food vending, fresh juice sales, freelancing and dropshipping are five business models identified as potential ways to grow KSh 10,000 into KSh 100,000 within a month.

Mitumba traders can source clothes from Gikomba and River Road for KSh 100 to KSh 300 and resell them online at KSh 600 to KSh 1,200, while food and juice vendors can target busy locations to generate daily profits of about KSh 3,300.

Smallholder farmers in Limuru and Karatina are deploying low-cost erosion-control methods ahead of the rains season.
They are undertaking these measures following devastating losses during the 2024 floods that killed more than 230 people and stripped farmland of fertile topsoil across the country.

Elizabeth Itotia, who farms five acres on a slope in Limuru, Kiambu County , estimates she lost KSh 200,000 worth of produce when the 2024 rains destroyed her kale, spinach, cabbage, potatoes, and indigenous vegetables.

The floods also stripped her fields of nutrient-rich topsoil, forcing her family to source replacement soil from other farms at additional cost and labour.
According to a report by The Associated Press, this season, Itotia has planted Napier grass and bamboo along erosion-prone sections of the farm, using the plants' root systems to stabilise the soil.
She has also placed sand-filled sacks inside shallow trenches to slow surface runoff. Her neighbour Esther Njoki has adopted a comparable method.

In Karatina, Nyeri County , coffee farmer Moses Muhoro is digging trenches and packing sacks with soil to limit runoff after the 2024 floods removed the productive topsoil from his land, reducing his coffee output the following season.

He recommended terracing, gabion construction, contour planting, and the use of cover crops as more permanent solutions and advised farmers to shift towards crops that can tolerate prolonged wet conditions, such as corn, wheat, and barley.
The timing of this season's rains is particularly sensitive because the short rains overlap with Kenya's corn harvest.

The latter two regions are among the country's principal food-producing zones, meaning significant losses there would carry national food security implications.

items.description: Dubai’s KHDA bars private-school teachers from using personal phones, WhatsApp or social media to contact students; approved platforms are now required too.

Dubai has banned education professionals in its private sector from using personal mobile phones, private WhatsApp accounts and personal social media profiles to communicate with students, requiring all contact to be conducted through institution-approved platforms.

The Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) announced the restrictions on November 13, 2026, as part of a new policy framework for safeguarding and learner protection in Dubai's private educational institutions.
The restrictions cover all adults working within KHDA-licensed and permitted institutions, including teachers, teaching assistants, coaches, volunteers and third-party contractors.

Foreign nationals form a large portion of this workforce, with Dubai's private education sector drawing educators from the United Kingdom, the United States, Canada, South Africa , India, the Philippines, Egypt and Jordan, among other countries.
The rules do not constitute a general ban on teachers using social media in their personal lives.
The restrictions specifically target communication between staff and learners through unofficial or private channels.
Under the framework, institutions must ensure all teaching-related communication takes place through approved devices and platforms, giving administrators oversight of staff-learner interactions.
Schools must also prohibit personal or secretive relationships with learners and enforce documented supervision arrangements for any one-to-one meetings.

Additional conduct requirements include prohibiting staff from accepting unauthorised gifts, ensuring interactions take place in visible environments where possible, maintaining professional boundaries in both physical and virtual settings, and observing institutional rules on photography and digital content involving students.

KHDA has granted institutions a phased implementation period of up to 12 months to review existing safeguarding policies, train staff and put the required oversight systems in place.
Requirements designed to provide immediate protection to learners are not subject to this transition window.

Institutions must also strengthen their safeguarding governance structures by appointing a Safeguarding Governor at board level alongside a Designated Safeguarding Lead or Child Protection Coordinator responsible for oversight and reporting.
The framework applies to virtual learning environments as well as on-site activities, meaning online interactions are subject to the same safeguarding standards.

All personnel must acknowledge their institution's Code of Conduct during induction, and the provisions also extend to learners aged 18 and above, with procedures adapted to adult consent and confidentiality requirements.
KHDA has indicated it will track compliance through its quality assurance activities and may take regulatory action against institutions that fail to meet mandatory requirements.

The new policy forms part of a broader push to strengthen learner protection across Dubai's private education sector, with the authority citing risks such as cyberbullying and online exploitation as key concerns driving the reforms.

In other news, Dubai introduced Law No. 4 of 2026, which took effect on August 26 , banning families and individual workers from sharing the same residential units and restricting shared accommodation to designated areas.

The regulations require at least five square metres of bedroom space per occupant, one bathroom for every four residents and separate bedrooms with private bathrooms for each household in family accommodation.

Violations attract fines ranging from AED 500 (approximately KSh 17,650) to AED 500,000 (KSh 17.6 million), with repeat offences potentially doubling the maximum penalty to AED 1 million, alongside possible licence cancellations and utility disconnections.

The changes could affect thousands of Kenyans among the estimated 30,000 to 50,000 living in Dubai, although existing shared housing remains permitted if it meets the new standards, with property owners given until August 26, 2027, to comply with the licensing requirements.

items.title: Ivy Njeri Maingi: The future of digital loyalty will be built on everyday value
items.description: Subscriptions create an ongoing relationship in which customers pay for access to a set of benefits over time.
content: The way Kenyans use digital services is changing. From ordering meals and groceries to booking rides and making payments, more of our everyday activities are moving onto digital platforms. But as these services become part of our daily routines, consumer expectations are changing too. Convenience is no longer enough. People want to know that the services they use regularly are giving them something meaningful in return.

This presents an interesting opportunity for businesses operating in Kenya’s digital economy. The next phase of growth will not simply be about getting more people to download an app or try a service once. It will be about earning a place in their everyday lives and giving them good reasons to keep coming back. One model gaining relevance in this conversation is the subscription service.

Subscriptions are changing the relationship between businesses and consumers. Rather than treating every purchase as a separate transaction, they create an ongoing relationship in which customers pay for access to a set of benefits over time. For businesses, this creates an opportunity to build loyalty. For consumers, it should mean greater convenience, more predictable value and a better experience.

But there is an important distinction, a subscription is only as good as the value it delivers. Consumers are becoming more deliberate about the digital services they pay for. They will question another monthly charge if the benefits are unclear or difficult to use. Businesses therefore have to move beyond simply packaging services together and demonstrate how a subscription makes everyday life easier or more affordable.

Kenya’s digital landscape provides a strong foundation for this shift. According to the Communications Authority of Kenya’s Q3 FY 2025/26 sector statistics, active mobile subscriptions reached 84.1 million, while mobile broadband consumption stood at 800 million GB during the quarter. The Media Council of Kenya’s Navigating the Digital Reality 26 report also found that 45.8% of respondents paid to access Kenyan digital content. While this is not a measure of subscription uptake across the economy, it points to a growing familiarity with paid digital experiences. The opportunity now is to make those experiences more useful and relevant to how people live.

At Bolt, this thinking informed the introduction of Bolt Plus in Kenya. We looked at how customers already use our platform: taking a ride to work, ordering lunch, buying groceries or making a last-minute change to their plans. These are not occasional activities for many of our customers. They are part of everyday life.

We asked ourselves how we could make those interactions more rewarding, particularly for people who use Bolt regularly. The answer was to bring together benefits that customers can use across rides and food and retail delivery in one subscription service.

For KES 280 a month, Bolt Plus subscribers receive 10% cashback on every eligible ride, free delivery on eligible food and retail orders, priority driver matching, faster food delivery and three free ride cancellations each month. New subscribers also get their first month free, with an annual subscription option available.

The thinking is not complicated. A customer takes a ride and earns cash back towards their next trip. They order food or groceries and save on eligible delivery fees. When demand is high, priority matching can make getting a ride more convenient. When plans change, they have more flexibility. These are small moments individually, but together they can make a meaningful difference to the overall customer experience.

This is also where subscriptions can play a role in shaping digital habits. When a service consistently delivers value, customers have more reason to return to it. Over time, the platform becomes a more familiar and useful part of how they organise their day. That is the kind of loyalty businesses should be working towards: not simply repeat transactions, but a relationship built on usefulness, reliability and trust.

For businesses, this requires a different approach to customer retention. Loyalty cannot be assumed because someone has downloaded an app or subscribed to a service. It has to be earned continuously. That means listening to customers, understanding how their needs evolve and making sure the benefits offered remain relevant.

It also means being transparent about what customers are paying for. Subscription services should not rely on complicated terms, hidden conditions or benefits that are difficult to access. The value proposition should be easy to understand, and the experience should live up to the promise.

There is a wider opportunity for Kenya’s digital economy here. As more services move online, businesses can think beyond individual transactions and build connected experiences around the needs of their customers. Mobility, food, grocery shopping and delivery may serve different needs, but they are all part of how people manage their everyday lives.
Ultimately, the success of subscription services will not be measured by how many people sign up alone. It will be measured by whether customers continue to find value in them.

At Bolt, we see Bolt Plus as one way of putting that principle into practice. We want customers to feel that the more they use the services they already rely on, the more value they get in return. Because lasting loyalty is not built by asking customers to come back. It is built by giving them a reason to.
Ivy Njeri Maingi, General Manager, Bolt Food Kenya

items.title: Kenya to push for infrastructure, AI investments after ITU re-election
items.description: Kenya is seeking more investments in last-mile connectivity and Artificial Intelligence for African countries after being re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication (ITU).
content: Kenya is seeking more investments in last-mile connectivity and Artificial Intelligence for African countries after being re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication (ITU).
Kenya was elected to the council after garnering 136 votes out of 173 during the election held at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) currently underway in Doha, Qatar.

In the policy statement delivered by Information, Communications and the Digital Economy Cabinet Secretary William Kabogo, Kenya called for affordable digital access through investment in last-mile connectivity and device affordability.

“Kenya has been a member of the Council since 1982. This renewed mandate lets us continue contributing to the governance of the Union, including its strategic and financial plans for 2028–2031,” said Kabogo via his official X handle.

According to GSMA, 63% of people in Africa are still not connected to the internet with the continent in need of $76.2 billion in capital expenditure to bridge the connectivity gap between 2025 and 2030.

Kenya is also backing partnerships that will help scale African AI capacity through investment in regional data centres, AI models that understand African languages, and data governance that protects African interests.
“On the Council, Kenya will work for affordable and meaningful connectivity, digital skills, trust in digital services, and a stronger African voice in global ICT policy,” he added.

Other priority areas for Kenya during its time in the council include equitable access to orbits and frequencies, and greater spectrum harmonization across Africa, implementing of adopted declarations.

As a member of the council Kenya now has a direct voice in decisions on spectrum, satellite orbits, standards and development assistance, which ultimately affect the cost of mobile data, the reliability of internet services and the pace of 5G expansion.

The re-election to the United Nations agency is also expected to help Kenyan telecommunications operators, internet service providers and startups gain early insight into emerging global standards and regulations in order to align their investment plans.

items.title: Gachagua opens DCP’s Nairobi office and vows free nominations ahead of 2027 polls
items.description: The Mt Kenya Times The Democracy for the Citizens Party leader used yesterday’s Nairobi launch to signal grassroots intent, promising smart-card membership, open nominations and no favoured candidates. By James Mwangi Rigathi Gachagua, leader of the Democracy for the Citizens Party, yesterday officially opened the party’s Nairobi County office, using the occasion to announce plans for a smart-card membership system and to pledge that the party’s 2027 nominations would be open, competitive and free of preferential treatment for any aspirant. The launch, held at a party meeting in Nairobi, marked the latest step in DCP’s accelerating effort to build a credible organisational presence in the capital ahead of what is shaping up to be one of Kenya’s most consequential general elections. “The DCP party will hold free and fair nominations, with smart cards for party members to be introduced soon,” Gachagua told those gathered. “There are no special individuals or favoured aspirants. I encourage all aspirants across the country to put their best foot forward and strengthen their grassroots networks ahead of the nominations in March.” The opening of a dedicated Nairobi County office carries significance beyond the symbolic. Nairobi is Kenya’s most populous county and its most politically volatile, a battleground where no single party has historically commanded undisputed loyalty and where the urban vote has repeatedly proven decisive in shaping national outcomes. For DCP, which has built its strongest foundations in Mount Kenya and Maasailand, establishing a visible institutional footprint in the capital represents a deliberate signal of national ambition. Gachagua was direct about what the new office represents. “Today, I was honoured to officially open our new DCP party office for Nairobi County,” he said. “This office is a statement of our commitment to serving Kenyans and strengthening our grassroots presence across the county and the country. We must continue listening to the people and acting on their wishes, as enshrined in Chapter One of the Constitution of Kenya: all sovereign power belongs to the people.” His remarks on party growth carried the confidence of a leader who believes the political tide is running in his direction. “Our party is the party of the moment and the future. We are growing every single day as we work to earn the mandate of the great people of Kenya,” he said, closing with a phrase that has become something of a DCP rallying call: “Green is wealth. Green is the future.” The timing of the Nairobi launch is not incidental. With the IEBC’s published electoral calendar placing party primary nominations between 17 March and 10 April 2027, and membership list submissions required by 16 March, the window for organisational preparation is narrowing faster than many in the political class appear to have fully absorbed. Gachagua’s announcement of a smart-card membership system — a move that would give DCP a verifiable, digitalised record of its membership base — suggests the party is thinking carefully about the administrative requirements of a credible nomination process, not merely the political theatre of rallies and launches. DCP has grown rapidly since its establishment. The party currently has three elected Members of County Assembly and one Member of Parliament among its ranks, and has attracted figures of political weight from both the Mount Kenya and Maasailand regions. It is widely regarded as one of the most consequential new political forces heading into 2027, with Gachagua himself described by analysts as a potential kingmaker whose endorsement could prove structurally decisive for any presidential candidate seeking a majority. The question of whether Gachagua will seek the presidency himself or transfer his support to another candidate — including DCP Secretary-General John Methu, whose name he has previously floated — remains publicly unresolved. Yesterday’s event offered no fresh clarity on that front. What it did offer was a portrait of a party leader investing seriously in the machinery of political organisation: offices, membership systems, open nominations and a constitutional framing of popular sovereignty that speaks to voters wary of elite deal-making. Whether DCP can translate that organisational investment into electoral dominance across a city as complex and competitive as Nairobi will be one of the defining tests of the party’s national credibility in the months ahead.   Some of the moments as captured in pictures

Deputy governor salary in Kenya: Basic pay, allowances and benefits explained
items.description: Learn about the Kenya deputy governor salary: see the KES 652,742 gross pay, estimated take-home, allowances, benefits, deductions and constitutional role details.
content: Kenya's deputy county governor earns a gross monthly salary of KES 652,742 under the current Salaries and Remuneration Commission (SRC) review cycle. This article breaks down the basic pay, allowances, deductions, and additional benefits that come with the office, and explains what the role actually involves.

The Salaries and Remuneration Commission (SRC) is responsible for reviewing and determining the salary of a deputy county governor in Kenya. Article 230(4)(a) of the Constitution gives the SRC authority to set remuneration for state officers at both national and county levels.

The Third Remuneration and Benefits Review Cycle, covering financial years 2021/2022 to 2024/2025, underpins the current pay structure. The gross monthly salary is KES 652,742 , made up of a basic salary of KES 391,645, a house allowance of KES 100,000, an official commuter allowance, and a salary market adjustment of KES 161,097.
The table below summarises the monthly pay structure for the current review period.

An upward revision was proposed for the 2024/2025 financial year, with the monthly gross rising from KES 652,742 to KES 684,233. Under the revised structure, a deputy county governor's basic salary moves to KES 410,540, with the house allowance remaining at KES 100,000.

Kenya uses a progressive PAYE tax system with five bands: 10% on the first KES 24,000 of monthly taxable income, 25% on the next KES 8,333, 30% up to KES 500,000, 32.5% up to KES 800,000, and 35% above that.

The mandatory statutory deductions from the deputy governor's salary are NSSF , SHIF at 2.75% of gross pay, the Affordable Housing Levy at 1.5% of gross pay, and PAYE income tax. A personal relief of KES 2,400 per month is then applied to reduce the final PAYE bill.
The table below shows an estimated monthly deductions calculation based on a KES 652,742 gross salary.
PAYE (on taxable income after pre-tax deductions)
Note: The PAYE figure is an estimate. The exact net pay depends on additional allowable deductions such as qualifying pension contributions. Contact KRA for a precise calculation.

Deputy county governors receive a monthly airtime allowance of up to KES 15,000. An annual leave allowance of KES 50,000 is also payable to both governors and deputy governors.

Governors and deputy governors are entitled to official vehicles with an engine capacity not exceeding 3,000cc. The county government is also obliged to provide an official residence with commensurate home utilities and attendants.

Annual medical coverage extends to the deputy governor, one spouse, and up to four dependent children below 25 years. The cover includes inpatient treatment of up to KES 10 million, outpatient cover of KES 300,000, maternity cover of KES 150,000, dental cover of KES 75,000, and optical cover of KES 75,000.
Deputy governors are eligible for a car loan of up to KES 5 million and a mortgage facility of up to KES 25 million.
Canada Clarifies Who Can Apply to Live in Its Rural Villages from 2027

Retirement benefits offer two options: a service gratuity equal to 31% of annual pensionable income for the period served, or participation in a pension scheme with employer contributions as determined by the SRC. Additionally, deputy governors receive group life and personal accident insurance coverage equivalent to three times their annual pensionable emoluments.
Any remuneration and benefits not specified in the SRC gazette notice are not payable unless subsequently set by the SRC.
Under the Constitution of Kenya, the county governor and the deputy county governor are the chief executive and deputy chief executive of the county, respectively.

When the county governor is absent, the deputy county governor acts as the county governor. Beyond that, the governor may assign the deputy governor any other responsibility or portfolio as a member of the county executive committee.
Constitutionally, the critical mandates of the deputy governor include deputising the governor, filling a vacancy in the governor's office, and promoting inclusivity in the county.

Despite earning over KES 600,000 monthly, many deputy governors have flagged that the majority are not included in the day-to-day management of counties, and have petitioned for legislative reforms. The Deputy Speaker of the Senate proposed the County Governments Amendments Bill 2024, which would allow deputy governors to chair county executive committee meetings, head disaster management, and provide oversight of service delivery units.

Each candidate for election as county governor must nominate a person who is qualified for nomination as county governor as the running deputy governor. This means the same eligibility criteria apply.
All requirements for the county governor apply equally to the deputy governor. These include:

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission does not conduct a separate election for the deputy governor; instead, the person nominated by the winning governor is declared elected alongside them.
A person shall not hold office as a deputy county governor for more than two terms.

After PAYE, SHIF, the Housing Levy, and NSSF deductions, the estimated take-home is approximately KES 420,500 per month. Beyond cash pay, the role comes with substantial benefits including medical cover of up to KES 10 million (inpatient), an official vehicle, an official residence, a car loan of up to KES 5 million, and a mortgage facility of up to KES 25 million. items.description: Kenyan coaches and PE teachers can apply for Germany’s fully funded 2027 ITK at Leipzig University, covering living costs; applications close 15 December 2026.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

The German Embassy in Nairobi has called on Kenyan sports coaches and physical education teachers to apply for the 2027 International Coaching Course (ITK), a fully funded postgraduate programme hosted by the Faculty of Sport Science at Leipzig University in Germany.

The programme runs in a hybrid format from June to December 2027, with online modules scheduled for June, July, and December, and an in-person residential phase at Leipzig University between August and November 2027.
It is financed by the Federal Foreign Office and the Ministry of Science, Culture and Tourism of the Free State of Saxony, as part of Germany's cultural promotion abroad.
17 Mastercard Foundations scholarships open for Kenyans to apply ahead of 2027 cycle
Participants choose one of four specialisations delivered in different languages: Sports for the Disabled in English, Football in French, Kids' Sports U12 in Spanish, and Basketball in Arabic.
PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.
Supporting modules cover general movement and exercise science, sports medicine fundamentals, sports didactics, project management, strength training, and inclusion in sports.
The funding package covers rent, health and accident insurance, tuition fees, and a public transport ticket in Leipzig.
These costs are deducted before the monthly grant is disbursed, with participants receiving the remaining balance as a living stipend.
The one expense participants must cover themselves is travel to and from Leipzig.
The ITK targets sports professionals from developing countries on the OECD's DAC list of ODA recipients, a category that includes Kenya.
Applicants must be aged 40 or below and hold an academic degree in sports.
Prior experience as active athletes, physical education teachers, or coaches is required, alongside a demonstrated capacity to handle physical and mental demands.
EU pays KSh 190k per month to Kenyans to study master's in Europe: How to apply
The application process involves two steps: registering through the programme's online portal and completing the required forms, then submitting all documents to the German Embassy in Nairobi.

The deadline for documents to reach Leipzig University is December 15, 2026, meaning Kenyan applicants should submit their materials to the embassy well ahead of that date to allow time for processing and transmission.
The German Embassy in Nairobi directed interested candidates to the link in its social media bio and the QR code on its post for further details and to begin the application process.

In other news, the European Union is offering Kenyan graduates fully funded master's scholarships under the Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters programme, providing a monthly stipend of €1,400 (approximately KSh 196,000) for up to 24 months.

The scholarship covers tuition and participation fees, health insurance, and contributions towards travel and relocation costs, with students studying at university consortia across multiple European countries.

Applications for the 2027–2029 intake are open through individual programme portals, with deadlines ranging from December 2026 to February 2027, including Neurasmus on December 1, EMMIR on December 20, GLOBE on January 4 and InterMaths on February 17.

Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree or recognised equivalent and submit documents such as academic transcripts, certificates, a CV, motivation letter and academic references, although individual programmes may impose additional requirements.

A TikTok post claiming that Joyce Wairimu Mbugua, the mother of the late Betty Bayo, had returned to Kenya from the United States, sparked a flurry of reactions over the weekend before her son moved quickly to set the record straight.

The post, captioned "welcome back mama Betty Bayo," showed Joyce, commonly referred to as Mama Betty, smiling indoors in a red sequin dress while holding a bouquet of red roses and white baby's breath flowers.

items.description: Kenyan Prince’s Lamborghini Urus and Mercedes-Benz GLE became trapped in Diani Beach sand after a show-off drive, hours after he denied repossession rumours.
content: PAY ATTENTION: TUKO is in WhatsApp Channels now! Subscribe and read news in your favourite messenger.

Kenyan forex trader and social media personality Raymond Omosa, popularly known as Kenyan Prince, turned a fun coastal outing into an expensive headache on Sunday, November 15, after driving two of his luxury cars onto the sand at Diani Beach.

The vehicles in question were his signature yellow Lamborghini Urus and a grey Mercedes-Benz GLE. What started as a moment to show off the cars to friends at the Coast ended with both machines buried wheel-deep in the sand, unable to move.
"We drove onto the beach to show off, and now we are stuck," Kenyan Prince told his TikTok followers in footage he posted himself that evening.

In the clips, Kenyan Prince appeared shirtless in patterned swim shorts as he surveyed the situation.
The videos showed tyres spinning helplessly, flinging sand in all directions while the cars sank further with each attempt to accelerate.
He and his friend Mushkerr, along with others in their group, tried pushing the vehicles free but had no success. The spinning only deepened the holes beneath the wheels.

Pointing to the Lamborghini, he noted the suspension had lifted off the ground entirely. "The Lambo's suspension is even floating, clearly showing that it is in the air. It is tough. Anyway, pray for us," he said.

After inspecting the tyres and the underside of one of the cars, he raised concerns about the damage caused. "You see, the spade has even destroyed my car's tyres, and those tyres to replace are around Ksh400,000. And you can see there is even a scratch," he said.

He concluded that only specialised recovery equipment would do the job. "The only way that car has to be lifted is with a winch. That is the easiest way," he added.

The timing of the incident added an extra layer of irony. Just hours before the cars got stuck, Kenyan Prince had posted a YouTube video from Mombasa pushing back against claims that his Lamborghini had been repossessed by auctioneers after footage of a Lamborghini Urus on a vehicle carrier had circulated online.
"Now we are here. You can see the Lambo was brought here safely, and I wonder if people still believe that it had been auctioned," he said in that video.

The day before, on Saturday, November 14, he had already drawn attention at a Mombasa petrol station after accelerating the Lamborghini at high speed near a crowd, nearly knocking over a bystander who had to leap out of the way.
As of Monday morning, Kenyan Prince had not shared any update confirming whether the two cars had been successfully winched out or what the full extent of the damage turned out to be.

Reactions online were largely amused, with many Kenyans treating the situation as a classic case of showing off gone wrong.
We also highlighted facts about Kenyan Prince’s challenge to Interpol and the US government, as the forex trader taunted officials from Dubai amid an international crackdown on alleged fraud.

At least 24 Kenyans have reportedly been arrested over a separate KSh 1.1 billion card fraud scheme, but authorities have not officially linked Omosa to the arrests. Despite the scrutiny, he told Interpol to “come for me here” and claimed he was “chilling in Dubai”.

items.title: Kenya, Italy strengthen security cooperation
items.description: Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen held bilateral talks with his Italian counterpart, Matteo Piantedosi, in Rome, culminating in the signing of an agreement to strengthen security cooperation between the two countries. The agreement establishes a framework for enhanced collaboration between Kenya and Italy in security, immigration and law enforcement, further enhancing the longstanding bilateral ties […]
content: Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen held bilateral talks with his Italian counterpart, Matteo Piantedosi, in Rome, culminating in the signing of an agreement to strengthen security cooperation between the two countries.

The agreement establishes a framework for enhanced collaboration between Kenya and Italy in security, immigration and law enforcement, further enhancing the longstanding bilateral ties between the two nations.

Murkomen elaborated that the discussions underscored the importance of strengthening collaboration in combating terrorism and its financing, transnational organised crime, illicit drug trafficking, human trafficking, migrant smuggling, cybercrime, maritime insecurity and other emerging security threats.

He added that the partnership will also open up opportunities for intelligence and security information sharing, specialised training, technical assistance, institutional exchanges, capacity building and the application of technology in addressing contemporary security challenges.

“Importantly, our cooperation will be anchored in respect for national sovereignty, constitutional principles, the rule of law and fundamental human rights. As we take this important step, our focus now shifts to the effective implementation of the Agreement through strengthened institutional coordination and sustained engagement”, he said.

The CS emphasised that Kenya values its friendship with Italy and remains committed to partnerships that advance national security, protect citizens and contribute to regional and international peace and stability.
He is accompanied by Amb. Fredrick Matwang’a, DIG- APS Gilbert Masengeli, and other officials from the ministry.

items.title: Kenya re-elected to ITU Council with Africa’s highest vote tally: What's our agenda, and what does it mean to local mwananchi?
items.description: Kenya has been re-elected to the ITU Council, one of the key policymaking organs of the U.N specialized agency for digital technologies and telecommunications.
content: DOHA, Qatar, 16th November, 2026 – Kenya has been re-elected to the Council of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), one of the key policymaking organs of the United Nations specialized agency for digital technologies and telecommunications.

The win came in a highly competitive contest, with 19 African countries vying for the region’s 13 Council seats under Region D to the 48-member Council, which runs the affairs of the ITU in between the Plenipotentiary Conferences.
Kenya garnered 136 out of a possible 173 votes in the election held at the ITU Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) currently underway in Doha, the highest number recorded by any African country.

Kenya’s campaign was led by the Cabinet Secretary for Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, Hon. William Kabogo Gitau EGH, who delivered Kenya’s policy statement at the opening ceremony, and led the country’s engagement with member states during the campaign on the sidelines of the conference, which opened on 9 November and runs until 27 November.
The ITU Council guides the implementation of the ITU’s strategy, oversees its budget and shapes priorities ahead of the next conference.

Membership gives Kenya a direct voice in decisions on spectrum, satellite orbits, standards and development assistance, which ultimately affect the cost of mobile data, the reliability of internet services and the pace of 5G expansion.
The Doha result continues a strong run for Kenya at the ITU, and reflects sustained progress at home and leadership abroad.
In its policy statement, Kenya set out the priorities it will now carry into the Council:

For ordinary Kenyans, this re-election has practical implications for everyday life. Kenya’s voice in regional spectrum allocation can help make devices more affordable and accelerate 4G and 5G rollout.

Stronger cooperation on undersea cables can reduce internet disruptions affecting mobile money, eCitizen and everyday browsing. Kenya’s push for inclusive AI also seeks to ensure that emerging digital tools work in Kiswahili and other African languages.

For Kenyan businesses and the ICT industry, continued representation gives operators, internet service providers and startups early insight into emerging global standards and regulations, helping them plan investments with greater confidence.

It also strengthens Kenya’s standing as a regional digital hub, reinforces investor confidence and creates opportunities for Kenyan engineers and experts to contribute to international ICT standards development.

With the seat secured, attention now turns to translating this influence into tangible outcomes, particularly ensuring Kenya’s proposals are reflected in the ITU’s strategic and financial plans when PP-26 concludes on 27 November.

Kenya will build on this momentum when it hosts the Internet Governance Forum in Nairobi from 14 to 18 December 2026, where it will champion regional action on undersea cable resilience, AI capacity and inclusive digital governance.

content: Principal Secretary for Medical Services, Dr Ouma Oluga, has called for collective ownership, institutional accountability and alignment of priorities as Kenya finalises the Kenya–US Health Cooperation Framework.

Dr Oluga urged health institutions, CEOs and technical teams to take responsibility for the framework’s risk assessment and mitigation plan, ensuring it reflects institutional realities and ongoing health reforms.
He emphasised that the process should identify vulnerabilities, strengthen institutional systems and address implementation risks, rather than serve as an audit or fault-finding exercise.

The PS also underscored the importance of diplomatic discipline, clear communication and safeguarding national interests, reaffirming the Government’s commitment to delivering quality healthcare to all Kenyans.
The framework presents an opportunity to strengthen institutional capacity, protect health reform priorities and advance a resilient, sustainable healthcare system.

items.title: Relief for Nairobi Residents as Mbagathi Adds More Diabetes Clinic Days
items.description: Dr Erica Koima, Mbagathi Hospital’s Medical Superintendent, said the extended clinic hours would ease access to care for patients who previously had to wait.
content: PAY ATTENTION: Mark TUKO.co.ke as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed!
NAIROBI, Kenya- Nairobi residents seeking diabetes care have received a boost after Mbagathi County Referral Hospital expanded its dedicated clinic from two days a week to five.
The move comes as the hospital, Nairobi City County and Novo marked World Diabetes Day with free screening and health education services targeting up to 400 community members.
Mbagathi’s diabetes clinic will now run from Monday to Friday and serves between 250 and 300 patients every month.

Residents who attended the World Diabetes Day event were offered free diabetes, hypertension, eye, foot and HbA1c checks, alongside HIV and tuberculosis screening.
Nairobi County expands newborn intensive care units to boost premature baby survival
The event was held under the theme, Early Action on Diabetes, highlighting the importance of knowing one’s status before complications develop.
Participants also received nutrition education and practical physical activity sessions led by a physiotherapist.
Dr Erica Koima, Mbagathi Hospital’s Medical Superintendent, said the extended clinic hours would ease access to care for patients who previously had to wait for limited clinic days.
The clinic operates through Mbagathi’s Centre for Driving Change in Diabetes, established under the iCARE partnership involving the hospital, Nairobi City County and Novo.
Walk-in patients can access services, while eligible Type 1 diabetes patients below 25 receive insulin support.
Jakob Mollerup, Novo’s General Manager for Middle Africa, said more than 800,000 people in Kenya are living with diabetes, with over half believed to be unaware of their status.
He said early testing, treatment and quality care were crucial in helping patients avoid severe complications.
Premature births account for 41% of newborn deaths in Nairobi, county expands care
Novo said its iCARE programme has set up more than 92 diabetes centres across Kenya, trained over 3,500 health workers and supported more than 6,100 people to access affordable insulin.
Nairobi County Director of Medical Services Dr Moses Owino said the fight against diabetes should continue long after World Diabetes Day.
People living with diabetes also shared their experiences, encouraging others not to fear diagnosis or abandon treatment.
Eric Omondi , who has lived with Type 1 diabetes for 23 years, said people diagnosed with the condition could still lead fulfilling and productive lives with the right support.
Health experts urged Kenyans to seek testing, especially if they experience increased thirst, frequent urination, unusual tiredness, unexplained weight loss or blurred vision.
They also encouraged people living with diabetes to remain physically active, eat healthy foods, take prescribed medication and attend regular clinic visits.

items.title: Nakuru to offer free veterinary services during animal health field day
items.description: Nakuru to offer free veterinary services during animal health field day Kenya News Agency
content: Nakuru County Government is set to conduct a free Animal Health Field Day aimed at improving animal health and welfare, preventing the spread of animal diseases, promoting responsible animal ownership and safeguarding public health.

The initiative will be implemented through the provision of essential veterinary services, bringing animal healthcare closer to residents, particularly pet owners and livestock keepers, while promoting preventive care and improving animal productivity.
The exercise, organised in collaboration with the Lions Club of Menengai, will be held at Baraka Estate Grounds in Rhonda Ward, Nakuru West Sub-County, on Thursday this week starting at 8:00 am.

According to Chief Officer for Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Veterinary Services, Dr. Michael Kiplangat Cheruiyot, the initiative is part of the county government’s commitment to improving animal health and ensuring residents have access to essential veterinary services.
“The initiative is part of our commitment to improving animal health and welfare while ensuring that residents have access to essential veterinary services,” said Dr. Cheruiyot.

He stated that by bringing these services closer to the people and offering them free of charge, the county government aims to encourage preventive animal healthcare, reduce the burden of animal diseases and promote responsible animal ownership.

Dr. Cheruiyot explained that during the exercise, free rabies vaccinations will be administered for dogs, cats and donkeys, while deworming services will be offered to dogs, cats, donkeys, sheep and goats.
In addition to that, castration services will also be available for dogs and cats.

The field day will further feature animal husbandry awareness sessions focusing on responsible dog keeping, proper animal care and disease prevention, with residents expected to benefit from information on practices that promote animal welfare and safer communities.
The Chief Officer noted that rabies prevention remained a critical component of animal healthcare, given the disease’s serious implications for both animal and human health.

He observed that rabies vaccination is an important preventive measure in protecting communities while encouraging residents to take advantage of this opportunity by bringing their animals for vaccination, deworming and other services.

Dr. Cheruiyot stated that the free Animal Health Field Day goal is to build healthier animal populations, protect public health and strengthen livestock productivity, which is an important pillar of household livelihoods and food security.
Rabies is a preventable but potentially fatal viral disease that can be transmitted from infected animals to humans, mainly through bites.
Vaccinating dogs and other susceptible animals is therefore an important strategy in reducing transmission risks and protecting communities.

Regular deworming is equally important in controlling internal parasites that can affect animal growth, health and productivity, while appropriate animal management practices help prevent diseases and improve animal welfare.
Beyond providing immediate veterinary interventions, the initiative highlights the importance of preventive animal healthcare in supporting the county’s agricultural development agenda.
Healthy livestock contributes to food security, household incomes and economic resilience, making investment in animal health an important aspect of improving the livelihoods of farming communities.

Through its Department of Agriculture, Livestock, Fisheries and Veterinary Services, the county seeks to strengthen veterinary service delivery, enhance disease prevention and control, improve livestock productivity and promote responsible animal husbandry practices.

The collaboration with the Lions Club of Menengai also demonstrates the importance of partnerships between government and community organisations in complementing efforts to improve animal welfare and extend essential services to residents.

The County Government has urged residents to turn up with their animals and take advantage of the free services, noting that preventive healthcare and responsible animal ownership are essential in building healthier communities.
